newsitem.title: UK: IBCA may raise Portuguese banks' L-term A ratings.
newsitem.headline: IBCA may raise Portuguese banks' L-term A ratings.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit agency, said on Wednesday it had put the long-term ratings of Portugal's Banco Portugues de Investimento (BPI), Banco Fonsecas & Burnay (BFB) and Banco de Fomento e Exterior (BFE) on RatingWatch with positive implications.
All three banks have a long-term rating of A and a short-term rating of A1. At the same time, IBCA upgraded the Legal ratings of BPI from 3 to 2 and BFB from 4 to 2.
BPI and BFB are both controlled by BPI-SGPS, the holding company for the Banco Portugues de Investimento group.
BPI recently acquired a 51 percent stake in BFE, previously controlled by the government, and its holding company has since acquired a further 14 percent stake in BFE.
A bid to acquire the outstanding shares in BFE was announced on Tuesday.
BFE is an investment and development bank which, in turn, controls a retail commercial bank, Banco Borges e Irmao (BBI).
The acquisition of BFE has more than doubled the size of the BPI group and as a result its position within Portugal's banking industry has changed significantly, IBCA said in a statement.
IBCA said it considered the Portuguese authorities would view the group on an integrated basis and that state support, were it required, would be available for both BPI and BFB.
"Although full details regarding integration have yet to be made public, on the surface BFE appears to represent a good fit for BPI," IBCA said.
Portugal's banking sector was highly concentrated and the need to increase market share had become all the more important, it said.

"The enlarged BPI will be well placed to compete and the outlook for the group remains favourable. A full analysis of BFE will be conducted once new management has finetuned details of overall group strategy," IBCA said.
